metadata.title: Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 2023: National report for England Volume 1

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report uses TIMSS 2023 assessment data for England, with pupils sampled through a two-stage design (schools, then classes within schools) and with replacement schools/classes used when needed. The achieved sample for England includes 4,091 year 5 pupils from 131 primary schools and 4,239 year 9 pupils from 136 secondary schools, with exclusions limited to pupils with significant special educational needs that would limit test participation and pupils unable to read/speak English. TIMSS methodology is designed for nationally representative estimates and includes procedures to reduce sampling error; the report notes that TIMSS sampling methodology uses jackknife repeated replication (JRR) for standard errors and confidence intervals. The manuscript also reports a non-response bias analysis and describes that non-response adjustment weights were used in that bias analysis (school and pupil weights with non-response adjustment components), but it does not provide the specific weight variable names in the extracted text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a national descriptive reporting document that reports TIMSS scale scores, benchmark attainment percentages, and domain/cognitive domain patterns rather than training or estimating a model with PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. The report does not describe any PV generation/combination procedure for England-specific analyses, and it does not document a missing-data handling strategy for an ML estimation pipeline. As a result, missing-data handling is not reported in the sense required for an empirical predictive analysis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: In England, all schools with pupils in year 5 and year 9 on 31 August 2022 were in the target population. Schools were excluded if they had small year groups (fewer than 9 pupils in year 5; fewer than 25 pupils in year 9), special schools, pupil referral units, and alternative provision schools. Within schools, pupil exclusions were kept to a minimum: only pupils with significant special educational needs that would limit them in following TIMSS instructions and pupils unable to read and/or speak English were excluded. The final analytic samples reported are 4,091 year 5 pupils from 131 primary schools and 4,239 year 9 pupils from 136 secondary schools, with participation meeting TIMSS criteria based on combined school/classroom/student participation rates (Criterion B) after replacement where needed.

data.outcome_summary: TIMSS 2023: National report for England Volume 1 summarizes England’s mathematics and science performance for two target year groups (year 5 and year 9) using TIMSS 2023 digital assessments administered online. The report describes a two-stage sampling approach (schools, then classes) and reports an achieved sample of 8,330 pupils across 267 schools (4,091 year 5 pupils in 131 primary schools; 4,239 year 9 pupils in 136 secondary schools). England’s pupils scored significantly above the TIMSS centrepoint (500) and above the 2023 international mean in both subjects and both year groups. The report also reports benchmark attainment patterns (advanced/high/intermediate/low) and domain results (mathematics content: number, measurement & geometry, data; science content: life, physical, Earth; plus cognitive domains: knowing, applying, reasoning). It further highlights trends over time (2003–2023) and notes that average performance can mask variation at the top and bottom of the distribution, with widening gaps driven largely by higher-performing pupils.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a national descriptive reporting report for TIMSS 2023 rather than an empirical machine-learning study. It does not specify any predictive modeling targets, algorithms, or model performance metrics, and it does not provide PV/missing-data handling details in the way required for an ML extraction. Therefore, ML technique fields and main findings are intentionally left empty, while survey design and assessment outcomes are summarized descriptively.
